entries.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
entries.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
entries.description: The original study claimed that let-7b expression was reduced in CD44-positive LAPC4 prostate cancer stem cells relative to CD44-negative cells; this replication tested the claim using FACS-sorted LAPC4 cells.
entries.citation_sentence: This experiment is comparable to what was reported in Figure 1B of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 3 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
entries.notes: The replication found let-7b underexpressed in CD44-positive cells, in the same direction as the original.

entries.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
entries.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
entries.description: The original study claimed that miR-34a expression was reduced in CD44-positive LAPC4 prostate cancer stem cells relative to CD44-negative cells; this replication tested the claim using FACS-sorted LAPC4 cells.
entries.citation_sentence: This experiment is comparable to what was reported in Figure 1B of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 3 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
entries.notes: The replication found miR-34a elevated rather than reduced in CD44-positive cells.

entries.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
entries.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
entries.description: The original study claimed that enforced miR-34a expression inhibited tumor regeneration and reduced LAPC4 xenograft tumor growth; this replication tested the claim by comparing miR-34a-transduced, negative-control-transduced, and untransduced LAPC4 cells in mice.
entries.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Supplemental Figure 5C of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 4 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
entries.notes: The replication found similar tumor weights and growth profiles across groups, with no statistically significant effect of miR-34a.

entries.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
entries.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
entries.description: The original study claimed that residual LAPC4 tumors showed no or only a marginal increase in miR-34a expression after miR-34a manipulation; this replication tested miR-34a expression in tumors derived from miR-34a-transduced LAPC4 cells.
entries.citation_sentence: The original study reported no, or marginal (~3X), increases in miR-34a expression in the residual tumors formed from prostate cancer cells, specifically LAPC4, LAPC9, and DU145, transiently transfected with miR-34a oligo compared to vector control (Liu et al., 2011).
entries.notes: No miR-34a was detected in tumors derived from miR-34a-transduced cells, but the authors noted that in vivo silencing prevented clear interpretation of the intended overexpression comparison.

entries.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
entries.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
entries.description: The original study claimed that CD44 expression was inversely correlated with miR-34a expression in tumors formed from miR-34a-transduced prostate cancer cells; this replication measured CD44 expression in tumors derived from miR-34a-transduced LAPC4 cells.
entries.citation_sentence: This experiment was described in Protocol 5 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015) and is conceptually similar to what was reported in Figure 4A of Liu et al. (2011), which used DU145 cells transduced with a retroviral vector encoding miR-34a.
entries.notes: CD44 expression did not differ between groups, but interpretation was limited because miR-34a was not detectable in the miR-34a-transduced tumors.

entries.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
entries.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
entries.description: The original study claimed that miR-34a directly repressed CD44 through putative miR-34a binding sites in the CD44 3-prime UTR; this replication tested wild-type and double-mutant CD44 3-prime UTR luciferase reporters in DU145 cells.
entries.citation_sentence: This is similar to what was reported in Figure 4D of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 7 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
entries.notes: The replication found no significant miR-34a effect on the wild-type reporter and described the results as not consistent in direction with the original study.
